<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command sources the PKGBUILD in a restricted context, executing only top-level code and not running any of the package functions (`prepare`, `build`, `package`, etc.). In this PKGBUILD, the top-level content consists solely of standard variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `arch`, `source`, `sha256sums`, etc.) and function definitions. None of these involve command substitution, immediate execution of external commands, or any side-effecting operations that could lead to data exfiltration or remote code execution during sourcing.

The `_install_icons` function is defined at the top level but is not invoked there; it is only called later within `package()`, which is outside the scope of `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Similarly, the `prepare()` and `package()` functions contain executable logic, but they are not executed during this phase. The `source` and `sha256sums` arrays reference a specific AppImage release from the project's GitHub repository, which is standard practice for binary packages.

There is no evidence of malicious code execution during the sourcing phase. All constructs used are part of normal PKGBUILD syntax and do not pose a risk when parsed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>No top-level execution risks in PKGBUILD</summary>
</security_assessment>
